shared_elements: T-shaped/broad-headed monolithic pillar or stele form
low-relief carving on a vertical stone surface
row of repeated arch/loop or U-shaped symbols along the upper zone
horizontal band separating upper register from lower imagery
animal figures rendered in profile relief
disc or circular motif on the body of the pillar
justification: Both surfaces show a broad-topped vertical pillar carved in low relief with a row of repeated arch/loop symbols across the upper zone, a horizontal dividing band beneath them, and further profile animal and sinuous serpentine forms plus a prominent disc below — a specific and non-obvious combination and ordering. The main differences lie in the specific creatures and details: B clearly includes a quadruped/predator, birds and a large long-necked bird-like figure in the lower register, whereas A's lower field is dominated by looping snake-like forms, paired discs and a belt-like band with a hanging element, so the individual motifs are not the same scene.
